scope: CPL, nonparametric and newest Lyman-alpha AP likelihood semantics for DESI DR2 dark-energy evidence; no new DESI or GU fit is performed.

primary_sources.observable_carrier: DESI DR2 BAO distance ratios combined with named CMB and supernova likelihoods
primary_sources.inference_map: observables and covariances -> CPL w0-wa posterior -> model comparison against Lambda-CDM
primary_sources.licensed_claim: Within the w0-wa extension, DESI+CMB prefers evolving dark energy at 3.1 sigma and DESI+CMB plus different supernova samples gives 2.8--4.2 sigma, with the preferred quadrant w0 > -1 and wa < 0.
primary_sources.ceiling: The posterior coordinates are model-conditioned fit parameters and are not literal pointwise measurements of a true w(z).

primary_sources.observable_carrier: the same named cosmological likelihoods evaluated through broader parametric and nonparametric dark-energy representations
primary_sources.inference_map: likelihood -> parametric and nonparametric reconstructions -> crossing and noncrossing class comparison
primary_sources.licensed_claim: Parametric and nonparametric routes both indicate possible phantom-divide crossing near z about 0.5; noncrossing alternatives are disfavored but cannot be ruled out.
primary_sources.ceiling: A crossing preference is not a class-wide exclusion, and CPL can approximate distances while failing to represent the underlying pointwise w(z).

primary_sources.observable_carrier: Lyman-alpha forest full-shape Alcock--Paczynski and BAO information centered at z=2.33
primary_sources.inference_map: high-redshift AP and BAO likelihood -> joint cosmological posterior with CMB and optionally supernovae
primary_sources.licensed_claim: The updated w0-wa comparison is 2.7 sigma for DESI+CMB and 3.2 sigma when supernovae are included.
primary_sources.ceiling: The high-redshift AP measurement updates the joint likelihood but does not by itself directly measure a low-redshift pointwise crossing.

rejected_inferences: CPL is a compression -> all crossing evidence disappears
the CPL central pair directly measures w(z) -> every noncrossing family is ruled out
precise_relocation: Treat the CPL posterior as model-conditioned compressed evidence; retain the direct and nonparametric lean toward crossing; evaluate an action-owned GU family against the underlying named likelihood before assigning a quantitative GU verdict.
dark_energy_07_corrections: 3.2 sigma is a two-degree-of-freedom Mahalanobis radius; the recorded one-dimensional reading is about 2.7 sigma
profiled f0 bounds are roughly three times looser than fixed-omega_m-h2 bounds
the honest discriminator is shape, not the bare +5.7 sigma_A amplitude overshoot; the recorded amplitude-marginalized shape penalty is +19.3 at M2=8 while fitted CPL gains -22.8
uncalibrated supernovae constrain distance shape and Omega_m, not H0 mechanically; calibrated GU Omega_m about 0.352 lies near the recorded DES-Y5 value
the theta family is excluded as the DESI dark-energy signal but unconstrained-but-null as a family, with best-f0 Delta AIC +1.9 to +3.2

historical_comparative_ledger.current_reuse_rule: Do not reuse its CPL central pair as a literal pointwise target. Preserve only the scoped likelihood lean that crossing models fit the named data combinations better until a GU family is tested directly.

corrected_evaluation_packet: derive one action-owned GU background, perturbation system and fixed initial data
derive the GU-family pointwise w(z) property rather than importing the CPL central pair
evaluate the current DESI DR2 BAO and Lyman-alpha AP, CMB and supernova likelihoods with their covariances and nuisance treatment
report CPL compression, nonparametric comparison and direct class-constrained likelihood separately
